meta.title: Operation of Polarizing Microscope in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To examine optical anisotropy (birefringence) of plant cell constituents including starch grains, calcium oxalate crystals, cellulose fibres, and lignified cells for identification and authentication of crude drugs.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for detection of starch grains (showing characteristic Maltese cross), calcium oxalate crystals, lignified elements, and polarization-active phytochemicals in crude drug powders and tissue sections.
procedure: Switch on the polarizing microscope and allow the halogen lamp to warm up for 5 minutes.
Insert the polarizer (lower filter) below the condenser into its designated slot.
Confirm the analyzer (upper filter) is retracted or set to the 0° (parallel) position initially.
Prepare the specimen: mount a thin powder smount in water or glycerine on a glass slide; apply a coverslip.
Place the slide on the mechanical stage and locate the specimen using bright field (analyzer out) at 10× first.
Cross the polars: rotate the analyzer to 90° — the background field should become completely dark (extinction).
Switch to the cross-polarized mode — birefringent structures (starch grains, crystals) will appear brightly coloured or white against the dark background.
Starch grains: look for characteristic Maltese cross (extinction cross) — confirms starch identity.
Calcium oxalate crystals: will appear bright white or coloured; identify crystal type (raphides, prisms, druses, styloids) for drug identification.
Rotate the stage — note the extinction angle and pleochroism for crystal identification.
Insert the red plate (first-order retardation plate) or gypsum plate if available to assist crystal identification through colour shift.
Systematically scan the powder mount and note the proportion, type, and size of polarizing structures.
Record observations with sketches or photomicrography using the camera port.
Remove the analyzer after observation and return the microscope to bright-field mode.
Clean the slide and stage after use; cover the microscope.
Log the drug name, structure observed, polarization behavior, and authentication conclusion in the register.
precautions: Handle the polarizer and analyzer filters with care — contamination or scratching of filter surfaces alters polarization quality.
Clean optical filters with lens paper only — never use regular tissue.
Ensure strict 90° crossing of polars for correct cross-polarized microscopy — incomplete crossing gives false birefringence patterns.
Do not apply too much pressure on the coverslip — stressed glass becomes birefringent, confusing results.
Use glycerine mountant for starch grain identification — water causes starch swelling and loss of Maltese cross pattern.
Keep the light intensity moderate — excessive intensity can cause fading of delicate coloured inclusions.
Store the polarizer and analyzer filters in their protective cases when not in use.
